Definition: probably akin to the base of G188 ("acid"); keen; by analogy, rapid:--sharp, swift.
BiblicalUsage: Sharp can describe a sword or swift feet. John saw a sharp twoedged sword going out of the mouth of the Son of man, and Paul said of the unrighteous that their feet are swift to shed blood.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sharp cuts both ways: the sword from the mouth of Christ is sharp, and the feet that run to shed blood are swift — I must know which side I am on.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
